sources.title: Generating high-quality Perturb-seq data for the 2026 Virtual Cell Challenge
sources.finding: Official data use consistent guides, time point and technology across cell lines, >=80% median target reduction, and 400 curated cells per intervention. Baseline similarity alone is not sufficient evidence of response similarity.
sources.action: Keep dose-normalized causal source responses and test whole-family transfer; do not tune from guessed context names.

sources.title: Perturbation response decomposition enables biologically aligned generalization to unseen perturbations and cellular contexts
sources.finding: The preprint separates global, context, conserved perturbation and context-interaction components. Generic response structure can dominate aggregate metrics, while context interactions are difficult to predict from control expression.
sources.action: Test a training-only perturbation-response subspace, rather than another control-expression autoencoder. V13 is an independent implementation inspired by the decomposition, not a reproduction of the paper.

sources.title: Tabular Foundation Models Are Competitive Cellular Perturbation Predictors Across Biological Scales
sources.finding: The preprint benchmarks general-purpose tabular models on several perturbation tasks and reports competitive performance against specialized architectures. These settings do not establish leaderboard gains for our zero-shot task.
sources.action: Prioritize transferable response features and rigorous held-context tests over architecture size.

sources.title: Replogle et al. 2022 raw RPE1 pseudobulk release
sources.finding: Author raw pseudobulk dataset verified against published MD5. Composite intervention IDs were explicitly parsed to HGNC symbols: zero intervention overlap with the 300 competition targets; 8,260 output genes overlap. Reproducible identifier audit and original coverage record retained.
sources.action: Retain coverage evidence and reproducible downloader; do not add generic RPE1 responses as direct evidence for unmeasured interventions.

limits: Technical papers and public participant claims do not supply hidden ABC responses or prove that a candidate will improve the leaderboard.
